title: Fairy Lights Bedroom Ideas: 5 DIY Projects & Placements
h1: Fairy Lights in the Bedroom: Placement Ideas and DIY Projects With Step-by-Step Instructions
description: Fairy lights bedroom ideas for above the bed, canopies, mirrors and windows, plus five DIY projects with steps, damage-free hanging tips and safety rules.
secondary_keywords: how to hang fairy lights in bedroom
excerpt: Headboard, canopy, mirror and window ideas for bedroom fairy lights, plus five step-by-step DIY projects and renter-safe hanging tips.
image_alt: Bedroom with warm fairy lights draped above the bed and glowing behind a sheer canopy
key_takeaways: Focus on one main feature: headboard, canopy, mirror or window.
Keep lights behind or above the headboard so they glow without shining in your eyes.
Use furniture like the headboard, bed frame and curtain rod to avoid wall damage.
Simple DIY projects such as a headboard halo or lit branch corner take under an hour.
Use LEDs only, keep plugs off bedding and put lights on a timer.

faq.q: How do you hang fairy lights above a bed?
faq.a: Mark three or five evenly spaced points 12 to 18 inches above the headboard, extending a little past each side of the bed. Attach small removable adhesive hooks at those points and drape the lights in shallow, equal loops of 4 to 8 inches. Route the cord down behind the bed to the outlet and add a dimmer.

faq.q: How do you hang fairy lights in a bedroom without damaging walls?
faq.a: Attach lights to furniture where possible, such as the back of the headboard, a four-poster frame, a mirror or the curtain rod. On walls, use removable adhesive hooks or clips on clean surfaces, spaced every 12 to 18 inches, and remove them slowly by pulling the tab downward. Tension rods work well inside window frames.

faq.q: Are fairy lights safe to have in a bedroom?
faq.a: LED fairy lights are generally safe in bedrooms when used correctly. Choose strings listed by a testing lab, never place lights or battery packs under bedding or pillows, keep plugs away from fabric, and use a timer so they switch off after you fall asleep. Replace any string with frayed wire or loose bulbs.

faq.q: What color fairy lights are best for a bedroom?
faq.a: Warm white lights around 2200 to 2700K are best for bedrooms. They create a soft, candle-like glow that suits winding down in the evening and blends with warm bedside lamps. Cool white or color-changing lights tend to feel harsher and more decorative than relaxing.

faq.q: How long should fairy lights be for a bedroom?
faq.a: A headboard halo or swag above the bed typically needs 16 to 33 feet of lights, a mirror frame 10 to 20 feet, and a canopy over the bed 33 to 66 feet. Measure the route, then add 20 to 30 percent for loops and reaching the outlet.
